description: GitHub Personal Access Tokens. Two coexisting kinds — pick `fine-grained` for new work (per-repo permissions, expiration), pick `classic` only when you need scopes the fine-grained model still can't express.

variants.description: Legacy `ghp_…` token. Account-wide scopes (`repo`, `admin:org`, `workflow`). Use only for tooling that hasn't migrated to fine-grained tokens yet — GitHub plans to retire classic PATs.

steps: Click Generate new token → Generate new token (classic)
Pick scopes (`repo`, `read:org`, `workflow` are the common ones)
Set an expiration — never `No expiration` for shared tooling
Click Generate token, copy the value (shown once)
retrieval.notes: Classic tokens grant access to ALL of your repos at the chosen scope. Prefer the fine-grained variant whenever possible — only fall back here when the workflow needs scopes (org-level admin, workflow billing) the fine-grained API still doesn't expose.

rotation.notes: Generate the replacement token, update every consumer, THEN delete the old one from Settings → Developer settings → Tokens. Both tokens stay valid until you delete the old, so there is no downtime window. GitHub also emails you before a token with an expiry lapses — treat that mail as the rotation trigger.

variants.description: Modern `github_pat_…` token. Per-repo scope, expiration mandatory, granular permissions. Default choice for new tooling.
variants.format_hint: starts with `github_pat_`, 82 chars of [A-Z0-9_] after the prefix

steps: Pick the resource owner (your account or an org you admin)
Limit to specific repositories — don't use `All repositories` unless you must
Pick the granular Repository permissions (Contents read/write, Pull requests, etc.)
Click Generate token, copy the value (shown once)
retrieval.notes: Fine-grained tokens cannot access org-admin or workflow billing scopes — those still require a classic PAT. For org-owned tokens, the org admin must enable fine-grained access in Org → Settings → Personal access tokens.

rotation.notes: A fine-grained token can be regenerated in place from its own settings page — `Regenerate token` keeps the same name, permissions, and resource list while minting a fresh value and resetting the expiry. The old value stops working immediately, so update consumers in the same change window. Prefer regenerate-in-place over delete+recreate to keep the permission set pinned.
